giga2003volume.title: Gigascope: A Stream Database for Network Applications (SIGMOD 2003, June 9-12, 2003, San Diego, CA) — the volume the AT&T backbone produced
giga2003volume.author: Chuck Cranor, Theodore Johnson, Oliver Spataschek, Vladislav Shkapenyuk
giga2003volume.quote: Even with the high degree of sampling and aggregation in Netflow records (traffic summaries produced by routers) the AT&T IP backbone alone generates 500 Gbytes of data per day (about ten billion fifty byte records).
supports: 500 Gbytes of data per day
about ten billion fifty byte records
AT&T IP backbone
this is already sampled and aggregated data, not raw packets

giga2003deploy.title: Gigascope: A Stream Database for Network Applications — conclusions, deployed scale at time of writing
giga2003deploy.author: Chuck Cranor, Theodore Johnson, Oliver Spataschek, Vladislav Shkapenyuk
giga2003deploy.quote: Currently we have seven installations, most of which proide special network monitoring services for AT&T customers. Our largest scale deployment monitors application protocol performance over two Gigabit Ethernet links for one of our customers. At peak periods, Gigascope processes 1.2 million packets per second using an inexpensive dual 2.4 Ghz CPU server. At the time of writing, this application has been running for three months nonstop. Additional deployments throughout AT&T, including OC48 deployments, are in negotiations.
supports: seven installations
1.2 million packets per second at peak, not sustained
inexpensive dual 2.4 Ghz CPU server
two Gigabit Ethernet links
three months nonstop

FURTHER deployments, including OC48 ones, were still in negotiations at the time of writing; the paper's abstract separately says Gigascope 'is undergoing installation at many sites within the AT&T network, including at OC48 routers', so the paper does not support 'in production on OC-48 backbone links'
'proide' is a typo in the printed paper

cm2003onesided.title: Improved Data Stream Summary: The Count-Min Sketch and its Applications (DIMACS Technical Report 2003-20, June 2003) — the one-sided error claim
cm2003onesided.author: Graham Cormode, S. Muthukrishnan
cm2003onesided.quote: The error bound here is one-sided, as opposed to all previous constructions which gave two-sided errors. This brings benefits for many applications which use sketches.
supports: the sign of the error was a deliberate design choice, stated as an advance over prior sketches
prior sketch constructions had two-sided error

cm2003theorem1.title: Improved Data Stream Summary: The Count-Min Sketch and its Applications (DIMACS Technical Report 2003-20) — Theorem 1, the point-query guarantee
cm2003theorem1.author: Graham Cormode, S. Muthukrishnan
cm2003theorem1.quote: Theorem 1. The estimate a-hat_i has the following guarantees: a_i <= a-hat_i; and, with probability 1 - delta, a-hat_i <= a_i + epsilon ||a||_1.
supports: the estimate is never below the truth
the overshoot is bounded by epsilon times the L1 norm of the whole vector, i.e. by total stream volume, not by the number of distinct keys
subscripts and hats transcribed from the PostScript; the printed form uses mathematical notation

cm2003params.title: Improved Data Stream Summary: The Count-Min Sketch and its Applications (DIMACS Technical Report 2003-20) — data structure and naming
cm2003params.author: Graham Cormode, S. Muthukrishnan
cm2003params.quote: It is named after the two basic operations used to answer point queries, counting first and computing the minimum next.
supports: the name Count-Min describes the algorithm: count into d cells, read back the minimum
the same section sets width w = ceil(e/epsilon) and depth d = ceil(ln(1/delta)), which rearranges to an overshoot of (e/w) x N

cm2003never.title: Improved Data Stream Summary: The Count-Min Sketch and its Applications (DIMACS Technical Report 2003-20) — heavy hitters, certainty from the one-sided error
cm2003never.author: Graham Cormode, S. Muthukrishnan
cm2003never.quote: Previous sketch methods gave probabilistic guarantees about outputting the heavy hitters. Here, there is absolute certainty that this procedure will find and output every heavy hitter, because the CM sketches never underestimate counts.
supports: no true heavy hitter can be dropped
false positives remain possible
the never-underestimate property is what upgrades a probabilistic top-K to a certain one

cmjalg2005.title: Crossref metadata record for DOI 10.1016/j.jalgor.2003.12.001 (the journal version of the Count-Min paper)
cmjalg2005.author: Crossref
cmjalg2005.quote: An improved data stream summary: the count-min sketch and its applications — Journal of Algorithms, volume 55, issue 1, pages 58-75, published-print 2005-04.
supports: the archival citation is Journal of Algorithms 55(1):58-75, published in print April 2005
OpenAlex records publication_year 2004 / publication_date 2004-02-05 for the same DOI, which is where the 2004 dating in some bibliographies comes from

unverified: That Gigascope itself used a Count-Min sketch. The SIGMOD 2003 paper describes GSQL operators and does not mention the sketch; the link asserted here is only that the same organisation, in the same year, faced the same per-flow-state problem.
That Count-Min was deployed on AT&T's production backbone monitoring. The tech report gives no deployment account, and the Gigascope paper lists OC48 deployments as still 'in negotiations'.
Any dollar figure for the AT&T monitoring programme. No source opened gives one; the cost carried in the prose is the data volume, which the Gigascope paper does state.
Chuck Cranor's and Theodore Johnson's individual roles within the Gigascope team beyond joint authorship.

That the conference version appeared at LATIN 2004. It is widely cited that way and the authors' own Count-Min Sketch site lists it, but no LATIN proceedings page or PDF was opened, so the claim is kept out of the prose and off the cards.

The exact publication date of the journal version. Crossref gives published-print 2005-04; OpenAlex gives publication_date 2004-02-05 for the same DOI. April 2005 (Crossref, print) is the figure used.

The text of the journal version (Journal of Algorithms 55(1):58-75) was not opened — it is paywalled. That it carries the same Theorem 1 as the tech report is inferred from the shared title and DOI, so the cards claim only that the tech report predates it, not that the two texts match.
